SUE Design Manager User Guide

Chapter 5

SUE Menus And Commands

SUE Menus

This section describes each menu item and command in the SUE Design Manager. A brief description of each command is displayed in the SUE Message Area when the cursor is over the menu item

File Menu

This menu is used create and open cells, save cells, import and export GDSII, and so forth. Each menu option is described below.

    Figure 13: File Menu 
     

New Schematic 

 Hotkey:Ctrl-n

This is used to create a new schematic. A form will pop up where you can specify the path and name of the new schematic, as shown in Figure 14.

    Figure 14: File Select Pop-up 
     

New Icon 

 Hotkey: None

This is used to create a new icon. A file navigator box will open which allows you to enter a name and directory path for the icon. If you already have an existing schematic and want to create an icon for it, use the Make Other View command from the View menu.

Open 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-l

Open/load an existing cell. A directory navigator box opens which allows you to search for the desired cell.

Save 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-s

Save the current cell. The cell will be saved in a file called <cell_name>.sue

Save As 

 Hotkey: None

Save the current cell under a new name. The current cell will be saved in a file called <cell_name>.sue and a copy of the cell will be saved with the new name.

Save and Descendents 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-w

Save the current cell and all modified subcells (cells in the hierarchy below the current cell) to disk.

Revert to Last Saved 

 Hotkey: None

Restore current schematic or icon to the version which was last saved.

Copy... 

 Hotkey: None

This will make a copy in memory of the current schematic. You will be prompted for a new cell name. Notice that this command does not save the new cell.

Write EDIF 

 Hotkey: None

Writes out the EDIF file for the current schematic. Refer to Appendix B, EDIF And SUE File Conversion for more details on EDIF conversion.

Change Path of Cell 

 Hotkey: None

This enables you to change the path to a cell's location.

Toggle Read Only 

 Hotkey: None

Allows you to set the Read-Only Status for an individually selected cell, or for all cells within a selected area. Options are displayed in Figure 15 below. If you Set... All Cells to be Read-Only, then all cells in memory and any new cells loaded will be read-only.

    Figure 15: "Read-Only Options" Pop-up 
     

Check File System 

 Hotkey: None

This option will run a diagnostic of all the icons and devices in your currently loaded schematic. Any errors will be displayed in the Warning window, as shown below.

    Figure 16: "Check File System" Message 
     

Print 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-t

Print current cell to a postscript printer or file. Print Setup (below) specifies which printer to use. If you select print to file, the file name will be in the format <cell_name>.ps.

Print and Descendents 

 Hotkey: None

Print the current schematic and all of its descendents. Schematics for primitives will not be printed. Refer to Print Setup for printing options.

Print Setup 

 Hotkey: None

This brings up a Print Setup pop-up form as shown in Figure 17. This allows you to specify the printer, orientation, number of pages per schematic, as well as other options.

To print to a printer larger than A-size, you need to set up the printer in your $MMI_LOCAL/sue/.suerc file. You add two statements per printer, as shown below: 

      set PRINT(B,SIZE) "11in 17in" 
      set PRINT(B,COMMAND) "lpr -Pbsizeprinter -r %s"


You also need a statement specifying the sizes of your printers: 

      set PRINT(PAGE_SIZES) "A B E F"
    Figure 17: "Print Setup" Sub-menu

Exit 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-d

Exits out of SUE. If cells have been modified and not saved, a warning pop-up will appear. If you need to save cells, select Cancel and save the cells before quitting.

Edit Menu

This menu manages basic object-creation functions, such as Cut, Copy and Paste, Add Wire, Line and Rectangle, Delete, Rotate, Flip, and so on. Each of the Edit Menu options is described individually.

    Figure 18: Edit Menu 
     

Undo 

 Hotkey: u

Undo last edit. There are 99 levels of undo.

Cut to Clipboard 

 Hotkey: Alt-x

Cuts (deletes) the selected object from the schematic or icon and stores it in the "Clipboard". You will then be able to Paste from Clipboard at a later time.

Copy to Clipboard 

 Hotkey: Alt-c

Duplicates the selected object and stores the copy in the "Clipboard" for pasting at a later time.

Paste from Clipboard 

 Hotkey: Alt-v

Pastes an object from the "Clipboard". Objects can be pasted into the current cell, or you can load a new cell and paste the object there.

Add Wire 

 Hotkey: w

Puts SUE into "Wire Mode" for drawing wires. Click Button-1 to start the wire, and it will follow the cursor. Click Button-1 again whenever you want a bend in the wire. Click Button-2 to end the wire.

After entering Wire Mode, the following keyboard commands apply:

  • Button-1 -Begin drawing a wire at the cursor position.

  • Ctrl-Button-1 - Begin drawing a wire at the closest connection (the one with the `X').

Once a wire is started, the following keyboard commands apply:

  • DEL or u - Undo last wire segment.

  • Button-1 - Start new segment (bend wire).

  • Ctrl-Button-1 or Double-Button-1 - End wire at closest connection (the one with the `X').

  • Ctrl-C - Abort wire mode, removing partially completed wires.

  • Shift - Holding down the Shift key while drawing a wire makes the wire all-angle (non-manhattan).

Add Text 

 Hotkey: t

Brings up a text cursor bar. Click on the desired location in the schematic, and type in your text. Click Button-2 to open a text size selection window. Text sizes are: very-small, small, standard, large and very-large. Click Button-3 to open a text anchor selection window. Text anchors can be: n, s, e, w, c, ne, se, nw and sw. The text anchor is the origin around which text will rotate and flip.

Add Line/Rect 

 Hotkey: l

Enables you to "draw" with straight lines, again using Button-1 to start and add a bend, and Button-2 to terminate. Lines can be drawn at any angle. Lines are not equivalent to electrical wires (see Wire Mode, above). Lines or rectangles are used to draw icons.

  • Clicking Button-1 will start a line.

  • Button-2/3 ends a line.

  • Ctrl-Button-2/3 ends the line with an arrowhead.

  • DEL - Will undo the last segment.

When you end a line, the line is still selected, and you are in the Line Edit Mode. While in Line Edit Mode, the following keyboard commands apply:

  • Holding down Button-1 over a marker (square dot at segment intersection) and moving the mouse will move that marker.

  • Holding down Shift-Button-1 over a marker and moving the mouse will move the entire horizontal or vertical segment.

  • Button-3 - When over a marker, will add a new marker near the current marker.

  • Shift-Button-3 - Deletes the current (highlighted) marker.

To draw a rectangle, hold down Button-2/3 and drag out the rectangle.

  • While drawing the rectangle, the Tab key toggles between sizing the rectangle and moving the rectangle.

  • Releasing the mouse button ends the rectangle.

  • When you end the rectangle, it is still selected, so you can edit it as described above for a line.

Add Arc 

 Hotkey: a

This allows you to draw an arc which is three-quarters of a circle or ellipse. Simply hold down Button-1, drag out the arc to the desired size, and release to end it.

Holding down and dragging Button-2/3 draws a circle instead of an arc. Once the arc or circle is drawn, you can edit it by clicking Button-1 over one of the markers. There are four markers: 2 control the arc size and shape, one controls the starting point for the arc, and one controls the end point for the arc.

Delete 

 Hotkey: q

Deletes the selected object(s). Undo (u) will restore.

Duplicate 

 Hotkey: d

Makes a duplicate of the selected object(s). The duplicated object(s) is selected, so you can move them to the desired location by clicking and dragging with any of the mouse buttons.

Rotate 

 Hotkey: r

Rotates the selected object(s) 90 degrees clockwise.

Flip Sideways 

 Hotkey: x

Flips the selected object(s) horizontally or sideways.

Flip Upside-Down 

 Hotkey: y

Flips the selected object(s) vertically or upside down.

Move 

 Hotkey: m

Allows you to adjust the position of the selected object(s) by dragging it into position. Holding down Shift-Button-1 (after selecting the Move command) constrains the move either horizontally or vertically. When objects are selected in SUE, you can hold down Button-2 to move them without executing the Move command.

Edit Properties 

 Hotkey: Double-Button-1

Brings up a sub-menu with the properties pertaining to the selected object.

For primitives (such as fets and globals) and instances, you can enter new properties, and they will be applied to the object when you click on Done. If you do not want to change the object's properties, click Cancel, as shown in Figure 19. For other objects such as text and lines, this puts you into Edit mode.

    Figure 19: "Edit Properties" Pop-up 
     

Edit Generator 

 Hotkey: Shift-Double-Button-1

Edit the selected Icon Generator. You first select the Icon Generator you which to edit and then click on Edit Generator. The form in Figure 20 will appear and allow you to make the changes.

    Figure 20: "Nand2" Pop-up 
     

Replace Instance 

 Hotkey: b

Replace the selected instance or instances with another instance in the current cell. The ports on the icon should be at the exact same location for Replace Instance to work properly. If the ports are not at the same location, then opens may be introduced into your schematic.

To use this command, first place an instance of the new cell into your schematic. For example, if you want to replace your A-size inverters with larger B-size inverters, place an instance of a B-size inverter into your schematic. Then, select the A-size inverters you wish to "upsize". (Remember, Shift-Button-1 adds to your selection.) Next, select Replace Instance and then click with Button-1 on the new instance (for this example, the B-size inverter).

Duplicate Text 

 Hotkey: Shift-t

Duplicates all selected text, including text inside an icon. You can then reposition this text in a new area. This saves much time when entering text labels in a series.

Lower 

 Hotkey: i

Lowers the selected object in the Display List to make it easier to select other nearby objects.

Modify Properties 

 Hotkey: None

Brings up the pop-up menu shown in Figure 21, and allows you to modify the specified property on all the selected instances.

For example, to change the width, `W', of the selected fets to 2.4, fill out the form as shown in Figure 21. YOu can specify a value in previous-value, and only change that property in particular selected instances with a specific value.

    Figure 21: "Modify Properties" Pop-up 
     

Name Objects 

 Hotkey: None

Brings up the sub-menu shown in Figure 22, and allows you to enter the naming pattern (prefix, suffix, direction, etc.) for the selected objects.

    Figure 22: "Name Selected" Pop-up 
     

Object Name Editor 

 Hotkey: None

Allows you to change the name of the selected object(s) in an editor.

First, select the instances you want to name, then select Object Name Editor. This will start a text editor in a new shell window. the editor that is started depends on the EDITOR environment variable. The example in Figure 23 has five instances selected (in this case, five nand gates) and rs using vi as the text editor.

    Figure 23: Object Name Editor 
     

Toggle Move Off-Grid 

 Hotkey: None

Permits you to move an object "off-grid" (not aligned to grid) by using the Control key as an on/off toggle, as shown in Figure 24.

    Figure 24: "Move Option" Pop-up Showing "Edit Move Off-Grid" Option 
     

Delete Buffer 

 Hotkey: None

Deletes the current edit buffer (the schematic or icon you are currently editing) from memory. Does NOT delete the associated Icon, Schematic or the disk file.

View Menu

The View Menu contains commands pertaining to detailed viewing of cells and schematics. Contains viewing aids such as Push Into and Pop Out Of, Zoom, Ruler measurement, and Grid set up. All the options are described in the following section.

    Figure 25: View Menu 
     

Push Into 

 Hotkey: e

Push into the schematic for the selected instance. If an instance is visible, it can be selected and pushed into for editing no matter how far down in the hierarchy it exists. You can also iteratively push down through the hierarchy. SUE remembers which cells you have pushed into so that when you use the Pop Out Of command it reverses the order of the Push Into commands. If there is no schematic for the selected instance, push into the icon view.

Pop Out Of 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-e

Pop back to the previous edit cell or the root (top level) cell.

Pop Connected 

 Hotkey: Alt-e

If a net or port is selected in the schematic, pop up to the calling schematic, select the net at this level, and zoom in on that net. For the example in Figure 26, a net was selected in the FA schematic and the Pop Connected command was executed.

    Figure 26: Example Of "View Pop Connected" 
     

Swap Views 

 Hotkey: c

This is a toggle button to switch between the schematic or the icon view of the current cell.

Swap Views Selected 

 Hotkey: Alt-s

This toggle switches views between the schematic and icon of a current cell. It maintains selection of any I/O's in the other view which were originally selected in the starting view.

Make Other View 

 Hotkey: Shift-c

This will create the associated schematic (if an icon is shown) or icon (if a schematic is shown) for the current cell. For the example shown in Figure 27, a schematic is started with ports a, b, c, cout, and sum . To finish the icon view, you could now use lines, rectangles, arcs and text to finish the icon.

    Figure 27: Example Of "View Make Other View" 
     

Zoom In on Cursor 

 Hotkey: j

Zooms in on the schematic or icon by 2X, centered around the cursor position. You must use the j hotkey for this command.

Zoom to Area 

 Hotkey: z

Zoom in to a specified region. Select Zoom to Area. Using Button-1, drag out a box around the region you want to zoom in on.

Zoom Out 

 Hotkey: Shift-z

Zoom out by 2X on the current cell. The window will remain centered.

Zoom to Fit 

 Hotkey: v

Zoom to fit the current cell in the display window.

Zoom to Fit Selected 

 Hotkey: Shift-v

Zoom to fit all of the selected object(s) in the window.

Pan 

 Hotkey: Shift-j

Moves the center of the layout to the current location of the cursor. For this command, it's best to use the hotkey. Move the cursor to the point in the layout you want centered on the screen and then use the hotkey Shift-j.

Select by Name 

 Hotkey: n

Select by Name brings up the pop-up form shown in Figure 28, which allows you to specify a net or instance name (wildcards - "*" - are okay). The net or instance must be in the current schematic. Search by instance type if you want to find all instances of a certain type..

    Figure 28: "Select By Name" Pop-up

.

Show Text Anchors 

 Hotkey: Shift-y

This option displays the anchor location(s) for all text within the current cell. The next time you select something, the anchors will be cleared.

Show Sel. Term Names 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-v

This displays the icon terminal names for the selected instances.

Show Inst. Origins 

 Hotkey: None

This option shows the origin locations for all the instances in the current cell.

Toggle Grid 

 Hotkey: g

This command toggles on or off the visibility of the grid.

Change Grid Spacing 

 Hotkey: Shift-g

This command brings up a popup form as shown below. The grid can be uniform (same in X and Y directions) or you can have different grid spacings, as shown in Figure 29.

    Figure 29: "Grid Spacing" Setup Form 
     

Ruler 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-r

Draw a ruler to measure distance. Button-1 starts the ruler and adds additional segments. Button-2 ends the ruler. Holding down the Shift key while moving the mouse toggles for non-manhattan rulers.

Ruler Setup 

 Hotkey: None

This opens the pop-up shown in Figure 30, where you can specify the mode and scale to use with the ruler.

    Figure 30: "Ruler Setup" Pop-up 
     

Display Cell Doc 

 Hotkey: Shift-d

Opens the file <cell_name>.doc or <cell_name>.html in an editor or browser window. If no documentation exists, it will prompt you to open a new file in your text editor (vi or emacs).

Sim Menu

The Sim Menu controls all the commands for Netlisting, Simulating, and Plotting of nets, as well as creating and manipulating Verilog properties, and cross-probing with the MAX Layout Editor.

The Sim Menu changes depending on which Simulation Mode you have selected. The various Sim Menu Modes are described in individual sections. The first section addresses command options which are common to all the Simulation Modes. Subsequent sections address each Simulation Mode individually. The DPC (Data Path Compiler) simulation mode is discussed in the DPC User Manual.

    Figure 31: Sim Menu 
     

Options Common To All Simulation Menus

<Simulator> Netlist 

 Hotkey: Shift-n

Create a netlist based on the selected simulation mode. You may choose from Verilog Netlist, SPICE Netlist, FLAT_SPICE Netlist, Sim Netlist, or DPC Netlist.

<Simulator> It 

 Hotkey: h

Run a simulator based on the selected simulation mode. You may choose from Verilog, SPICE, FLAT_SPICE, or Sim.

Init Probe 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-i

Initialize, or re-initialize, the simulator probe. This will have different functions based upon the simulation mode.

Close Probe 

 Hotkey: None

Closes any existing probe window or program.

Change Simulation Mode 

 Hotkey: None

Brings up a pop-up where you can change the simulation parameters for Netlist Type and Properties, as shown in Figure 32.


Each sub-menu of the Netlist Type in the Change Simulation Mode pop-up will be listed in detail individually, at the end of this section.

    Figure 32: "Change Simulation Mode" Pop-up 
     

The Properties field specifies which property to use in the icon for netlisting. Refer to Figure 33, the icon view for a pmos icon. The three properties on the bottom specify how to netlist for SPICE, Verilog, and Sim. Notice that when you change simulation mode to flat_spice, the Property is "spice". It will use the spice property for netlisting.

You would use the No Header option when you want a netlist without the header, for example, a SPICE netlist for LVS.

    Figure 33: Example Of pmos Icon 
      


 
     

Change Probe Type 

 Hotkey:None

Opens a selection box for you to choose between simulation probes (for example, different waveform viewers). Different probe types will be available depending upon which Netlist Type you have selected.

Display Design Hierarchy 

 Hotkey:None

Displays the design hierarchy of the currently selected cell in a small information window, as shown in Figure 34. This feature is mainly used for Verilog simulations.

    Figure 34: "Display Hierarchy" Example 
     

Generate Term Names 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-g

This option computes netlisting information for the current cell, without writing out the netlist. It reports any potential netlisting problems.

Create Verilog Property 

 Hotkey: None

This option automatically creates a "verilog-netlist" text string for an icon. You can modify the text by clicking on it with Button-1, using the Backspace or Delete keys to erase text, and then type in your changes. Click Button-2 over the text to bring up a selection box for text size. Click Button-3 to bring up a selection box for text orientation.

Edit Verilog 

 Hotkey: Shift-e

This brings up a window with the Verilog .vb file for the selected instance in your text editor. If nothing is selected, then it displays the .vb file for the current cell. If there is no Verilog file, you will be promted to create a new Verilog file.

When SUE creates a new Verilog file, it creates a template which includes the port section. If you have added, deleted or changed the name of any ports in your schematic, SUE will query whether you want SUE to automatically update the ports section of your Verilog model. You will need to manually update the actual Verilog for this cell.

Load Verilog I/O's 

 Hotkey: None

A file window will open where you can select the name of a textual Verilog file. Click Done, and the Verilog I/O's will be placed into the current SUE schematic.

Change Simulation Mode: "verilog"

    Figure 35: "verilog" Netlist Type Selected in Change Simulation Mode Pop-up

From the Change Simulation Mode pop-up, selecting the option "verilog" accesses the Sim menu shown in Figure 36:

    Figure 36: The "Verilog" Sim Menu 
     

VERILOG Netlist 

 Hotkey: Shift-n

Generate a Verilog netlist for the current schematic.

VERILOG It 

 Hotkey: h

This command first writes out a Verilog netlist for the current cell. Next, it either starts up Verilog in interactive mode, or runs Verilog simulation and starts a waveform viewer.

Init Probe 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-i

Initialize, or re-initialize, the simulator probe (an interactive simulation or a waveform viewer). If you are doing interactive simulation, Verilog is started, and you can now interactively simulate the design.

Init Probe w/Options 

 Hotkey: None

Start interactive Verilog simulation with the specified options.

Close Probe 

 Hotkey: None

Closes any existing probe window or program. For interactive simulation, this exits the Verilog simulation. For waveform viewers, this command closes the viewers.

Change Simulation Mode 

 Hotkey: None

Brings up a pop-up where you can change the simulation parameters for Netlist Type and Properties, as shown in Figure 35.

Change Probe Type... 

 Hotkey:None

Opens a selection box for you to choose between interactive Verilog simulation, SignalScan, or SimWave waveform viewers.

Display Design Hierarchy 

 Hotkey:None

This command displays the design hierarchy of the currently selected cell in a small information window, as shown in Figure 37. This window not only displays the design hierarchy, but more importantly, allows you to control where behavioral models should be used. If there is no underlying schematic for an icon, SUE automatically looks for the behavioral model, which can either be included in the icon, or in a separate text file. If the window is blank, click on Netlist to netlist the schematic, and display the hierarchy information.

    Figure 37: Display of Design Hierarchy 
     

By default, SUE stops and uses a behavioral model when it finds the Verilog property (-type auto -name verilog...) in the icon for the cell. This can be changed in two ways.

  • First, in the Display Design Hierarchy pop-up, you can have SUE look into a lower level schematic for netlisting. If you see a "-I" in front of a cell name, this means that the icon view is being used for netlisting (therefore, the behavioral model) but that there is an underlying schematic for this cell.

    In the example in Figure 37, adder8 is such a cell. If you click with Button-1 on the cell in the pop-up and then click on Netlist, SUE will use the schematic for that cell when netlisting. In Figure 37, shift8 is a cell where the schematic for the cell is used for netlisting, instead of the behavioral model.

  • The second way to control netlisting is by adding the following property into the icon for a cell. 

          -type fixed -name netlist_level -text 2000

    This will ignore the Verilog property on this icon for netlisting, and use the underlying schematic instead.

Change Simulation Mode: "spice"

    Figure 39: "spice" Netlist Type Selected in Change Simulation Mode Pop-up

From the Change Simulation Mode pop-up, selecting the option "spice" accesses the Sim menu shown in Figure 40. Note that this section references HSPICE, but you can use any SPICE simulator.

    Figure 40: The "SPICE" Sim Menu 
     

SPICE Netlist 

 Hotkey: Shift-n

Generates a hierarchical SPICE netlist for the current schematic. the SPICE property in the primitives or lowest level cells tells SUE how to netlist for SPICE.

SPICE It 

 Hotkey: h

This command does three things:

  1. Writes out a SPICE netlist for the current cell.

  2. Runs your SPICE simulator (for example, HSPICE). Refer to Appendix C for details on how to set up your SPICE interface.

  3. Starts the NST Waveform Viewer. NST is the waveform viewer included with SUE.

You will now be able to select nets in SUE and view the waveform for that net in NST. Refer to the NST documentation for more details on how NST works.

If the waveform viewer does not appear, be sure to look at the SUE command window (the shell window from which you started SUE). It will tell you if there were problems netlisting or running HSPICE. Often, the problem is that an HSPICE license was not available.

Init Probe 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-i

Start the NST waveform viewer and load the HSPICE output file (the .tr0 file). If you have run SPICE outside of SUE, you can use this option to load the output file.

Close Probe 

 Hotkey: None

Closes the NST waveform viewer window.

Change Simulation Mode... 

 Hotkey: None

Brings up a pop-up where you can change the simulation parameters for Netlist Type and Properties, as shown in Figure 38.

Select Simulator 

 Hotkey: None

Opens a list of pre-installed SPICE-like simulators for you to choose from. The form in Figure 41 appears, allowing you to select from different SPICE simulators, such as ADM (Star-Sim, from Avant!) or PowerMill. Change the suffix of the output file to .sw0 or .ac0 if you are doing other than transient simulations.

    Figure 41: Change Simulator Form 
     

Change Probe Type... 

 Hotkey:None

Opens a selection box for you to choose between waveform viewers. NST is the waveform viewer included with SUE.

Display Design Hierarchy 

 Hotkey:None

Displays the design hierarchy of the currently selected cell in a small information window. This feature is generally used for Verilog simulation.

Generate Term Names 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-g

This option computes netlisting information for the current cell, without writing out the netlist. This is a quick way to find out if there are any netlisting problems. After running this command, you can determine how SUE named any unnamed nets or instances.

Back Annotate Caps 

 Hotkey: None

This option will back-annotate the capacitances from a Sim file generated by MAX onto the current cell.

MAX Cross Probe Init 

 Hotkey: None

This initializes the cross-probing between SUE (schematics) and MAX (layout). You must run MAX Cross Probe Init before you can run MAX Cross Probe.

When you select this command, the pop-up shown in Figure 42 will appear. It lists all the MAX sessions currently running on your computer. If you already have the corresponding cell loaded in MAX, select that copy of MAX. Otherwise, you can start a new copy of MAX.

The Max executable for new max specifies which command to execute to run MAX. You may have a shell wrapper script that gets executed at your site. If you have multiple monitors on your computer, X display for new Max controls the initial MAX startup monitor. Finally, Max technology controls the technology for MAX startup.

If MAX cannot find a matching layout cell, <cell_name>.max, it gives you the option to either search for the MAX file, or open a new cell. If you open a new MAX cell, you can then use the MAX Layout Generator to help generate the layout. Please refer to the MAX User Guide for more details.

    Figure 42: MAX Cross-probe Pop-up 
     

Max Cross Probe 

 Hotkey: k

This highlights the net in the MAX layout which corresponds to the selected net in the current SUE schematic.

Kill Spice Job 

 Hotkey: None

This searchs for and "kills" (aborts) any previously launched SPICE simulation job. You will not be able to run a new simulation if there is a previous one still active.

Plot Net 

 Hotkey: p

This command instructs the simulation probe to plot the currently selected net in the NST waveform viewer.

Unplot Net 

 Hotkey: o

This command instructs the simulation probe to un-plot the currently selected net in the NST waveform viewer. This is equivalent to "erasing" the probe.

Plot Net & Remember 

 Hotkey: Shift-p

The probe will plot the selected net and keep a copy of the plot in memory to use in future simulations. The next time you run SPICE and bring up the NST waveform viewer, this net will automatically be plotted.

Unplot Net & Forget 

 Hotkey: Shift-o

This instructs the simulation probe to un-plot the selected net, and not to plot it again for any future simulations.

Plot Old Net 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-p

This instructs the probe to plot the selected net, but to use the data from a previous simulation (if this data is loaded). To use this command, first load the <cell_name>.tr0~ file in NST. This file contains the results from your previous SPICE run.

Unplot Old Net 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-o

This instructs the probe to un-plot the selected net, using the data from a previous simulation.

Erase and Plot Memory 

 Hotkey: None

Clear the simulation probes and re-plot remembered nets.

Cancel Memory 

 Hotkey: None

Purges memory of all remembered nets.

Create Verilog Property 

 Hotkey: None

This option automatically creates a Verilog property text string for an icon.

Edit Verilog 

 Hotkey: Shift-e

This brings up a window with the Verilog .vb file for the selected instance. If nothing is selected, then it displays the .vb file for the current cell. Refer to the Verilog Sim menu for more details.

Load Verilog I/O's... 

 Hotkey: None

Change Simulation Mode: "flat_spice"

From the Change Simulation Mode pop-up, selecting the option "flat_spice" accesses the Sim menu shown in Figure 44:

    Figure 44: The "FLAT_SPICE" Sim Menu 
     

FLAT_SPICE Netlist 

 Hotkey: Shift-n

Generates a flat SPICE netlist for the current schematic. The SPICE Property in the primitives or lowest level cells tells SUE how to netlist for SPICE.

FLAT_SPICE It 

 Hotkey: h

This command does three things:

  1. Writes out a FLAT_SPICE netlist for the current cell.

  2. Runs your SPICE simulator (for example, HSPICE). Refer to Appendix C for details on how to set up your SPICE interface.

  3. Starts the NST Waveform Viewer. NST is the waveform viewer included with SUE.

You will now be able to select nets in SUE and view the waveform for that net in NST. Refer to the NST documentation for more details on how NST works.


You will only be able to plot top-level nets in NST if you have done a FLAT_SPICE simulation

If the waveform viewer does not appear, be sure to look at the SUE command window (the shell window from which you started SUE). It will tell you if there were problems netlisting or running HSPICE. Often, the problem is that an HSPICE license was not available.

Init Probe 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-i

Start the NST waveform viewer and load the HSPICE output file (the .tr0 file). If you have run SPICE outside of SUE, you can use this option to load the output file.

Close Probe 

 Hotkey: None

Closes the NST waveform viewer window.

Change Simulation Mode... 

 Hotkey: None

Brings up a pop-up where you can change the simulation parameters for Netlist Type and Properties, as shown in Figure 43.

Select Simulator 

 Hotkey: None

Opens a list of pre-installed SPICE-like simulators for you to choose from. The form in Figure 41 appears, allowing you to select from different SPICE simulators, such as ADM (Star-Sim, from Avant!) or PowerMill. Change the suffix of the output file to .sw0 or .ac0 if you are doing other than transient simulations.

Change Probe Type... 

 Hotkey:None

Opens a selection box for you to choose between waveform viewers. NST is the waveform viewer included with SUE.

Display Design Hierarchy 

 Hotkey:None

Displays the design hierarchy of the currently selected cell in a small information window. this feature is currently used for Verilog simulation.

Generate Term Names 

 Hotkey: Ctrl-g

This option computes netlisting information for the current cell, without writing out the netlist. This is a quick way to find out if there are any netlisting problems. After running this command, you can determine how SUE named any unnamed nets or instances.

Back Annotate Caps 

 Hotkey: None

This option will back-annotate the capacitances from a Sim file generated by MAX onto the current cell.

MAX Cross Probe Init 

 Hotkey: None

This initializes the cross-probing between SUE (schematics) and MAX (layout). You must run MAX Cross Probe Init before you can run MAX Cross Probe.

When you select this command, the pop-up shown in Figure 42 will appear. It lists all the MAX sessions currently running on your computer. If you already have the corresponding cell loaded in MAX, select that copy of MAX. Otherwise, you can start a new copy of MAX.

The Max executable for new max specifies which command to execute to run MAX. You may have a shell wrapper script that gets executed at your site. If you have multiple monitors on your computer, X display for New Max controls the initial MAX startup monitor. Finally, Max technology controls the technology for MAX startup.

If MAX cannot find a matching layout cell, <cell_name>.max, it gives you the option to either search for the MAX file, or open a new cell. If you open a new MAX cell, you can then use the MAX Layout Generator to help generate the layout. Please refer to the MAX User Guide for more details.

Max Cross Probe 

 Hotkey: k

This highlights the net in the MAX layout which corresponds to the selected net in the current SUE schematic.

This searchs for and "kills" (aborts) any previously launched SPICE simulation job. You will not be able to run a new simulation if there is a previous one still active.
